sources.title: Antiqua et Nova. Note on the Relationship Between Artificial Intelligence and Human Intelligence
sources.author: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and Dicastery for Culture and Education
sources.abstract: The Vatican's doctrinal note on what separates artificial intelligence from human intelligence, with guidance on work, education, healthcare, warfare, and relationships.

sources.title: Magnifica Humanitas. Encyclical Letter of His Holiness Pope Leo XIV on Safeguarding the Human Person in the Time of Artificial Intelligence
sources.author: Pope Leo XIV
sources.abstract: The first papal encyclical devoted to artificial intelligence. Reads the whole tradition of Catholic social teaching into the AI age: dignity, work, truth, freedom, and the refusal to treat machines as persons.

sources.title: Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church
sources.author: Pontifical Council for Justice and Peace
sources.abstract: The systematic summary of Catholic social teaching: the human person, the common good, solidarity, subsidiarity, work, economic life, and political community. The foundation the AI documents build on.

sources.title: The Rome Call for AI Ethics
sources.author: RenAIssance Foundation
sources.abstract: The Vatican-convened pledge on AI ethics signed by tech companies, governments, and religious leaders. Six principles: transparency, inclusion, responsibility, impartiality, reliability, security and privacy.

sources.title: No, AI Isn't Conscious. But Saying So Invites Further Discernment
sources.author: Joshua Hochschild
sources.abstract: A philosopher at Mount St. Mary's University examines Magnifica Humanitas' denial of AI consciousness, notes that the encyclical asserts rather than argues the point, and shows how the classical tradition can supply the missing argument while taking seriously what interpretability research is finding inside these models.

sources.title: Pope Leo XIV Addresses the International Catholic Legislators Network
sources.author: Pope Leo XIV
sources.abstract: An address to Catholic lawmakers where Pope Leo XIV calls for legislation that balances technological innovation with human rights, warns against AI creating new dependence and 'ideological or economic colonialism,' and names the family as the primary cell of society that AI must never be allowed to erode by reducing persons and relationships to data and simulations. Closes with the line: 'the world does not need an artificial intelligence that diminishes humanity; rather, it needs human intelligence enlightened by wisdom.'
